stem: $ABCD$ is a kite with $AB = AD$ and $CB = CD$. The diagonals intersect at $E$. $A\hat{B}E = {=z}^\circ$ and $B\hat{C}E = {=c}^\circ$. Calculate the size of $A\hat{D}C$, in degrees.
solution: The diagonals of a kite intersect at right angles, so $B\hat{E}C = 90^\circ$.
The angles of $\triangle BEC$ add up to $180^\circ$: $E\hat{B}C = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - {=c}^\circ = {=t}^\circ$.
$E$ lies on the diagonal $AC$, inside $A\hat{B}C$, so $A\hat{B}C = A\hat{B}E + E\hat{B}C = {=z}^\circ + {=t}^\circ = {=ans}^\circ$.
One pair of opposite angles of a kite is equal. The unequal sides meet at $B$ and at $D$, so $A\hat{D}C = A\hat{B}C = {=ans}^\circ$.
notes: Advanced: a multi-step angle chase that uses the right-angled diagonals, the angle sum of a triangle, adding two adjacent angles at B, and the equal pair of opposite angles. Check: with BAE = 90 - z and BCE = c, the angles of triangle ABC are 90 - z, c and z + 90 - c, summing to 180, so every (z, c) in range is a real convex kite. The answer also equals (360 - A - C)/2 with A = 180 - 2z and C = 2c, so a solver using the angle sum of the quadrilateral agrees.
